title: Fusion Project Timelines vs Historical Energy Technology Deployment
executive_question: How does fusion's expected development timeline compare to the historical deployment of fission, solar, and wind?
required_metrics: Year of first grid-connected plant (fusion projects: ITER, SPARC, DEMO, private startups)
Year of first commercial plant (fission: 1954 Obninsk, 1957 Shippingport; solar: 1954 Bell Labs, 1980s utility-scale; wind: 1970s early turbines, 1990s commercial farms)
Years from first demonstration to 1% of global electricity (for each technology)
comparison_set: Fusion projects (ITER, SPARC, DEMO, Helion, TAE, etc.) vs. historical fission, solar PV, and wind energy deployment milestones.
preferred_sources: IEA World Energy Outlook for renewables
search_queries: first nuclear power plant grid connection 1954
data_quality_rule: Use official project timelines and historical records. If a fusion project has no firm date, note as 'target' or 'estimated'. Do not extrapolate beyond announced dates.
narrative_role: Establishes the historical context for fusion's timeline, supporting the argument that fusion will not be commercial before 2035.
pre_exhibit_context: Before showing this timeline, the report claims that fusion is not coming soon and that 2035 is optimistic. This exhibit grounds that claim in historical precedent.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Fusion's timeline is longer than the deployment of fission and renewables, reinforcing that grid-scale fusion is unlikely before 2035.

title: Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) Projections: Fusion vs. Alternatives
executive_question: At what cost can fusion compete with solar, wind, gas, and fission, and when?
required_metrics: Year (annual from 2025 to 2050)
LCOE ($/MWh) for fusion (range: low, high)
LCOE ($/MWh) for solar PV (utility-scale)
LCOE ($/MWh) for onshore wind
LCOE ($/MWh) for natural gas combined cycle
LCOE ($/MWh) for nuclear fission
comparison_set: Fusion vs. solar PV, onshore wind, natural gas, and nuclear fission LCOE projections.
preferred_sources: Lazard Levelized Cost of Energy Analysis (annual)
Company investor presentations (e.g., Commonwealth Fusion Systems cost targets)
search_queries: IEA World Energy Outlook 2024 LCOE projections
data_quality_rule: Use published LCOE estimates from authoritative sources. For fusion, use ranges from multiple companies and independent studies. Mark projections as 'estimated' if not firm. Require at least 4 annual data points per technology.
narrative_role: Quantifies the cost competitiveness of fusion under different scenarios, supporting the hypothesis that fusion LCOE may remain above $50/MWh by 2040.
pre_exhibit_context: The report argues that fusion's market viability depends on cost. This exhibit shows projected LCOE ranges for fusion and competing technologies over time.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Fusion LCOE is projected to decline but may remain above solar and wind costs through 2040, limiting its market share unless carbon pricing or other factors intervene.

title: Annual Private and Public Fusion Investment by Country (2015-2025)
executive_question: Where is fusion investment flowing, and which countries are leading?
required_metrics: Country/region (US, EU, China, Japan, Other)
Investment amount ($ million) – private (venture capital, corporate)
Investment amount ($ million) – public (government R&D budgets)
comparison_set: Private vs. public investment by country/region over time.
search_queries: EU fusion research funding Horizon Europe
data_quality_rule: Use official budget documents and industry reports. Cross-reference Crunchbase with company announcements. For 2025, use announced budgets or estimates. Mark as 'preliminary' if not final.
narrative_role: Shows the scale and trend of fusion funding, supporting the hypothesis that private investment will exceed $10B cumulatively by 2025 and that government funding is increasing.
pre_exhibit_context: The report discusses capital flows and government support. This exhibit provides the data on investment trends.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Private fusion investment has grown rapidly, led by the US, with significant government funding from the US, EU, China, and Japan. Cumulative private investment likely exceeds $10B by 2025.

title: Tritium Supply-Demand Balance for Fusion Reactors (2030-2060)
executive_question: Is tritium availability a showstopper for large-scale fusion deployment?
required_metrics: Tritium supply (kg/year) – from CANDU reactors, other sources
Tritium demand (kg/year) – based on number of fusion reactors and consumption per reactor (e.g., 0.1 kg/GW-year)
Number of fusion reactors (projected)
comparison_set: Tritium supply vs. demand under different reactor deployment scenarios (low, medium, high).
preferred_sources: Company disclosures on tritium breeding plans
search_queries: tritium supply CANDU reactors kg per year
tritium consumption per fusion reactor kg per GW
data_quality_rule: Use IAEA data for tritium supply. For demand, use engineering estimates from peer-reviewed studies. Mark projections as 'estimated' and include a range. Require at least 4 annual data points.
narrative_role: Highlights a critical resource constraint that could limit fusion deployment, supporting the need for tritium breeding technology.
pre_exhibit_context: The report examines technical risks. This exhibit shows the projected tritium supply from existing sources vs. demand from planned reactors.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Without effective tritium breeding, fusion deployment will be severely constrained by tritium supply, potentially limiting the number of reactors that can operate.

title: Fusion Startup Survival: Number of Active Companies (2015-2030)
executive_question: How many fusion startups will survive to commercialization?
required_metrics: Number of active fusion startups (with public milestones)
Number of startups that have ceased operations or been acquired
comparison_set: Active startups vs. cumulative failures/ acquisitions over time.
preferred_sources: News articles on fusion company closures
data_quality_rule: Define 'active startup' as one that has raised at least $1M and has a public roadmap. Use multiple sources to track status. For future years, use projections based on current trends. Mark as 'estimated' after 2024.
narrative_role: Supports the hypothesis that the number of fusion startups with a credible path will decline to fewer than 10 by 2030 due to consolidation and failures.
pre_exhibit_context: The report discusses competitive dynamics and consolidation. This exhibit shows the trend in active fusion startups over time.
post_exhibit_takeaway: The fusion startup landscape is consolidating; many early-stage companies may fail or be acquired, leaving only a handful of credible players by 2030.

title: Fusion LCOE Sensitivity to Key Variables (2040 Scenario)
executive_question: Which variables most affect fusion's cost competitiveness?
required_metrics: Variable (capital cost $/kW, capacity factor %, discount rate %, fuel cost $/MWh, O&M $/MWh)
LCOE ($/MWh) – base case and range
Sensitivity (change in LCOE per unit change in variable)
comparison_set: Impact of each variable on LCOE (bubble size = relative impact).
search_queries: fusion capital cost per kW estimate
data_quality_rule: Use published sensitivity ranges from credible sources. If not available, use typical ranges from fission or other technologies as proxies, clearly labeled. Do not invent data.
narrative_role: Illustrates the uncertainty in fusion LCOE and identifies key drivers, supporting the need for sensitivity analysis.
pre_exhibit_context: The report notes that fusion LCOE estimates are highly uncertain. This exhibit shows how changes in key inputs affect LCOE.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Fusion LCOE is most sensitive to capital cost and capacity factor; improvements in these areas are critical for competitiveness.

title: Public Acceptance of Fusion vs. Fission: Survey Results (2020-2024)
executive_question: Is public acceptance of fusion higher than fission, and does it vary by region?
required_metrics: Region (US, EU, China, Japan, Global)
Percentage of respondents who support/ oppose fusion energy
Percentage who support/ oppose nuclear fission (for comparison)
comparison_set: Fusion vs. fission support/ opposition by region and year.
preferred_sources: Academic studies on public perception of fusion
data_quality_rule: Use nationally representative surveys with sample sizes >1000. Report margin of error. If only one survey exists, note that. Do not combine different survey methodologies without adjustment.
narrative_role: Provides evidence on public perception, supporting the hypothesis that fusion faces less opposition than fission but still local siting challenges.
pre_exhibit_context: The report discusses regulatory and social license risks. This exhibit shows survey data on public opinion.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Public acceptance of fusion is generally higher than fission, but a significant minority remains opposed, and local siting may still face challenges.
